name: আদি বরাহ পেরুমাল মন্দির, তিরুক্কল্বনুর (কামাক্ষী অম্মন মন্দিরের অভ্যন্তরে)
deity: আদি বরাহ রূপে বিষ্ণু, কল্বর পেরুমাল, দণ্ডায়মান, দেবী অঞ্জিলৈ বল্লী নাচিয়ার-এর সঙ্গে — কামাক্ষী অম্মন মন্দিরের ভিতরের একটি দিব্য দেশম্ মন্দির
period: তোণ্ডৈ নাড়ুর একটি দিব্য দেশম্, তিরুমঙ্গৈ আলবার কর্তৃক নালায়িরা দিব্য প্রবন্ধমে গীত
dynasty: কাঞ্চি কামাক্ষী অম্মন মন্দিরের অভ্যন্তরস্থ একটি মন্দির
summary: তিরুক্কল্বনুর কোনো আলাদা মন্দির নয়: এটি কাঞ্চিপুরমের কামাক্ষী অম্মন মন্দিরের ভিতরে আদি বরাহ, কল্বর পেরুমালের একটি ছোট বিষ্ণু মন্দির, এবং তিরুমঙ্গৈ আলবার কর্তৃক গীত একটি দিব্য দেশম্।

sections.history: Thirukkalvanur is unusual among the 108 Divya Desams of Thondai Nadu, because it is not a temple of its own. It is a Vishnu shrine inside the Kanchi Kamakshi Amman temple, set on the right side of the Goddess's sanctum, and pilgrims who come to the Kamakshi temple worship the lord here as well. Thirumangai Alvar sang the shrine in a single verse of the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, naming the place Thirukkalvanur. The lord is Adi Varaha, known locally as Kalvar or Kalvan Perumal, and his consort is Anjilai Valli Nachiyar. Devotional references name the Vamana Vimanam over his sanctum and the Nithya Pushkarini as his tank.
sections.architecture: Because the shrine lies within the Kamakshi Amman temple, it shares that temple's gateways, courts and pillared halls rather than having its own. It is a small sanctum on the right of the Goddess's shrine, where Adi Varaha stands facing west with Anjilai Valli Nachiyar. Devotional references name the Vamana Vimanam as its vimana and the Nithya Pushkarini as its tank. The temple's priests or attendants can direct you to the shrine.
sections.legends: The name comes from the Tamil kalvan, a thief, and tradition tells the story in more than one way. In one, Lakshmi fondly called the lord Kalva when he came to her secretly. In another, Vishnu hid behind a pillar to overhear a conversation between Kamakshi and Lakshmi, and Kamakshi noticed him there. The versions differ, but each makes the lord a gentle thief of hearts, quietly present beside the Goddess of Kanchi.
sections.festivals: The shrine shares in the life of the Kamakshi Amman temple around it, whose festivals draw crowds through the year. Vaikunta Ekadashi is the customary observance at Divya Desams; confirm dates, and what is observed here, locally.
sections.experience: Visit it as part of a darshan at the Kamakshi Amman temple: after seeing the Goddess, look for the Vishnu shrine on the right side of her sanctum. It is small and quiet, and the playful story of the lord who hid behind a pillar gives it its charm. Pilgrims of the Divya Desams count it among Kanchipuram's shrines of the lord.

visit.timings: Darshan is through the Kamakshi Amman temple, so its daily schedule applies. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: The shrine lies inside the Kamakshi Amman temple in Kanchipuram town. Kanchipuram has a railway station and is reached by road from Chennai; Chennai International Airport is the nearest major airport. Enter by the Kamakshi temple and ask for the Vishnu shrine.
